problem: Pretrained diffusion navigation policies (NavDP) are limited by offline data coverage and imitation gives no explicit safety enforcement, causing insufficient obstacle clearance, oscillation and failures in narrow passages. Existing RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies relies on value/critic estimation, which is unstable, high-variance and memory-hungry.
motivation: Navigation foundation models give strong zero-shot priors but need safe, robust behavior beyond the offline training distribution. A critic-free approach with an analytical geometric reward from onboard RGB-D can adapt them cheaply and stably.
key_idea: Fine-tune the pretrained NavDP diffusion policy with trajectory-level GRPO, scoring groups of sampled trajectories with an analytical occupancy/inflated-occupancy reward instead of a learned critic, and updating only a small parameter subset and the final denoising steps.
insight: Per the ablations, selective fine-tuning (keeping the backbone frozen) and restricting updates to the final denoising steps are both important for effective adaptation, preserving pretrained geometric priors. Group-relative comparison of sampled trajectories with a hand-built geometric reward removes the need for a value network.
method: Task formulation: PointGoal navigation cast as goal-conditioned short-horizon trajectory generation with pretrained NavDP.
Trajectory-level GRPO: sample a group of trajectories per observation and use group-relative advantages to update the policy, with no critic.
Analytical reward: computed from local occupancy and inflated-occupancy grids derived from onboard RGB-D, penalizing collisions and insufficient clearance.
Selective fine-tuning: only a small subset of policy parameters is updated while the rest of the backbone stays frozen.
Final-denoising-step updates: RL updates restricted to the last denoising steps of the diffusion process.

setting.backbone: NavDP (diffusion navigation policy, partially fine-tuned with GRPO)
setting.training_data: Pretrained NavDP weights, then RL fine-tuning in Isaac Sim scenes with analytical occupancy-based reward (scale not given in abstract)
setting.action_space: predicted short-horizon trajectories (waypoints) from diffusion policy
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (also zero-shot transfer to Habitat)
setting.privileged: none at test time (reward uses onboard RGB-D-derived occupancy during training)

numbers.extra: held-out Isaac Sim scenes; baseline pretrained NavDP SR 0.520, SPL 0.490
numbers.evidence: Abstract: 'improves Success Rate from 0.520 to 0.587 and Success weighted by Path Length from 0.490 to 0.537 on held-out scenes'

numbers_note: abstract only; real-world Go2 success rate 70% not tied to a benchmark entry; Habitat transfer numbers not given.
results: On held-out Isaac Sim scenes, SR improves from 0.520 to 0.587 and SPL from 0.490 to 0.537 over pretrained NavDP, also outperforming representative diffusion-policy RL alternatives. It retains OOD geometric generalization, transfers zero-shot to Habitat, and reaches 70% real-world success on a Unitree Go2 with safer behavior.
limitations: Modest absolute gains (about +6.7 SR points); evaluated mainly in simulation with limited real-world trials
Reward is purely geometric (occupancy-based) and only handles PointGoal navigation; no semantic or language goals
